item.text: {"search_note":"I found some evidence of measurement and standardized delivery, but not strong evidence of transparent correction loops like published service-performance failures, independent audits, or policy reversals based on public feedback. The pro evidence is mostly internal bureaucratic reporting or government self-report, so it does not establish a robust evidence-and-correction culture.","evidence":[{"title":"Special social payments for medical workers were routed through the Social Fund","publisher":"Government of the Russian Federation","date":"9 Jan 2023","url":"https://government.ru/en/news/47503/","summary":"The government said payments for primary-care, ambulance, rural, and remote-area medical staff would be calculated from hours worked and administered through the Social Fund using electronic employee lists and portal notifications. This is real bureaucratic measurement and delivery, though it is not transparent public correction.","question_ids":["6B.5","6B.4","6B.2"]},{"title":"Single-stream child benefits for families with children","publisher":"Government of the Russian Federation","date":"9 Jan 2023","url":"https://government.ru/en/news/47503/","summary":"The same package centralized lump-sum family benefits into a single payment stream starting 1 Jan 2023. That shows standardized administration and some measurement of eligibility, but not independent monitoring of service quality.","question_ids":["6B.5","6B.4","6B.2"]},{"title":"Rosstat wage monitoring for teachers, doctors, and social workers","publisher":"Rosstat","date":"2024","url":"https://rosstat.ru/storage/mediabank/itog-monitor_04-2023.htm","summary":"Rosstat published 2023 wage monitoring for social-sector workers, indicating a functioning statistical apparatus that tracked inputs into social services. This is evidence of measurement, but only weak evidence of corrective management.","question_ids":["6B.5","6B.4"]},{"title":"2023 education-service delivery retrospective","publisher":"Government of the Russian Federation","date":"2024 retrospective on 2023","url":"https://government.ru/en/news/51246/","summary":"The government reported nearly 3,000 school buses delivered, free hot meals for all primary pupils, and teacher bonus pay. This suggests some monitoring of delivery outputs, but the source is official retrospective reporting rather than transparent external correction.","question_ids":["6B.5","6B.2","6B.4"]},{"title":"Access to economic statistics was restricted; corruption was pervasive","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2023","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2023","summary":"Freedom House says the state restricted access to economic statistics and used dubious takeovers and tax penalties while corruption remained pervasive. That points against transparent correction and toward opaque, captured administration.","question_ids":["6B.5","6B.4","5B.10"]},{"title":"Schools and teachers were ordered into patriotic instruction","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2023","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2023","summary":"Freedom House says schools and teachers were required to run patriotic-education classes, use state-sanctioned war language, and comply with military directives, with dissenting educators punished. That is evidence of political control over a service system, not evidence-based correction.","question_ids":["6B.5","6B.1","6B.4"]},{"title":"Personalist rule and patronage shaped governance","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2023","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2023","summary":"Freedom House describes Putin’s system as personalist, with civil society folded into pro-state tasks and government support coming with strings attached. That is broad background evidence against neutral, professionally corrected service management.","question_ids":["6B.5","6B.4","6B.1"]},{"title":"Weak accountability for public administration","publisher":"U.S. Department of State","date":"22 Apr 2024","url":"https://www.state.gov/reports/2023-country-reports-on-human-rights-practices/russia","summary":"The State Department says authorities jailed critics, closed NGOs, restricted media, and left impunity intact for security personnel. That implies weak independent oversight and little real correction pressure on the state.","question_ids":["6B.5","6B.1","6B.4"]}]}
